congregados.name: Congregados Basilica
congregados.short: A Baroque Oratorian church with a façade by André Soares; its second tower was finished only in 1964
congregados.long: The Oratorian friars laid the foundation of the church in 1703 and it was blessed in 1717. The façade, designed by André Soares, was built in 1761–1766, but the towers and statues were left unfinished. The west tower was completed only in 1964, paid for by the patron Nogueira da Silva. Since 1975 the church has held the title of minor basilica.
congregados.history:
The Congregation of the Oratory of Saint Philip Neri came to Braga in 1686 at the invitation of Canon João de Meira Carrilho. The friars built a house and a college, and in 1703 they laid the foundation of the church, with the master builder Manuel Fernandes da Silva in charge of the work. With the permission of Archbishop Rodrigo de Moura Teles, the church was blessed on 27 October 1717.

The façade was designed by André Soares, the leading architect of Baroque Braga. The Galician stonemason Paulo Vidal built it in 1761–1766. Soares also drew the choir arch, the organ case and the altar of Our Lady of Sorrows. But the façade stayed unfinished: one tower stood without its dome, and the other rose only halfway. In 1769 the Marquis of Pombal ordered the church closed, and it did not reopen until 1777.

In 1834 the religious orders were abolished in Portugal, and the Oratorians’ house passed to the state. It held a public library, a lyceum and later a teacher training school; today the building houses the music department of the University of Minho. Since 1845 the church has served the Brotherhood of Our Lady of Sorrows. On 14 July 1944 a small plane clipped the east tower with its wing and crashed; the pilot was killed.

The façade was completed only in the 20th century. The patron António Augusto Nogueira da Silva paid for the west tower, designed by the architect Alberto da Silva Bessa; it was finished in 1964. That same year statues of Saint Philip Neri and Saint Martin of Dume, by Manuel da Silva Nogueira, were raised into the niches of the façade. On 15 March 1975 the Holy See gave the church the title of minor basilica.
facts: The church was founded in 1703 and blessed on 27 October 1717.
The façade, designed by André Soares, was built in 1761–1766.
The west tower was finished only in 1964.
In 1944 a plane clipped the east tower with its wing and crashed.
A minor basilica since 1975; a Property of Public Interest since 1993.
congregados.tip: The basilica stands on Avenida Central, five minutes’ walk from Republic Square. Entry is free. A hundred metres across the road is the Nogueira da Silva Museum, founded by the man who paid for the west tower. The façade is beautifully lit in the evening.
